title: Independent ideas. Extraordinary finds.
intro: A daily selection of independent games and useful Android apps, with original F7 insights and links to their creators.

entries.name: El Almojarife
entries.summary: A maritime trading game set on the Iberian and North African coast in the 15th and 16th centuries. You found a merchant house and run it as a business: buy cargo in one port, sail it somewhere it is scarce, then reinvest in hulls, crews, warehouses and city property. The build is an explicit beta, and the developer documents which betas actually ship binaries.
features: Trades 20 goods across 33 cities while markets move and stock runs out, so a route that paid last voyage may not pay twice
Sells you rumours and dockside price reports and leaves unvisited ports genuinely unknown instead of hiding the same data behind a menu
Automatic routes support multi-stop buy and sell rules, price limits and a cash reserve you decide not to touch
Shipyards sell hull repairs, equipment, captains and convoys, and weapons occupy cargo space you have to budget for
Warehouse stewards buy only up to a stock target, sell only above a floor you set, and can lock outflow during a voyage
entries.insight: Trading games usually solve their own history by handing the player a complete map. El Almojarife prices information as cargo: a run to Huelva is profitable because you paid to learn something about it, which turns bookkeeping into exploration.

entries.name: Late Eastern Han Dynasty
entries.summary: A grand strategy game set in 190 CE, when the Han court had lost its grip and warlords rose across thirteen provinces. It calls itself a playable prototype rather than a release, and the loop it demonstrates is the classical one: govern, gather officers, campaign, fight and claim a title.
features: Develops agriculture, trade and city walls, recruits and trains troops, and keeps a population fed through drought and winter
Appoints officers along three parallel career tracks — civil, military and nobility — and raises officer families across generations
Assembles armies with a commander, deputy commanders, an adviser and five-position squads before marching roads and besieging cities
Resolves battles three ways: automatic summary, standard close combat, or tactical hex control, plus single duels
Documents 27 interlocking systems, including hidden attributes, faction politics and fame, treasure equipment and relationship webs
entries.insight: Chinese historical strategy normally reaches players through commercial series. This prototype rebuilds the same loop in the open and publishes an asset manifest that names the author and licence of every screenshot and font, keeping commercial character art out of the build entirely.

entries.name: The Human Box

price.label: Free, no install for the browser build

entries.summary: A live emergent simulation of Stone Age tribes that runs in a browser tab and needs no install. Nothing is scripted: individuals are born with traits mixed from both parents, learn by reinforcement, and inherit a slightly mutated copy of their mother's decision table, her vocabulary and her attitudes to other tribes.
features: Simulates an 800 by 400 tile world across ten biomes with elevation, rivers, lakes, weather and four seasons
Lets tribes invent their own languages, lineages, cultures and wars instead of climbing a authored tech tree
Gives about 160 tools in five categories — life, nature, resources, deadly and world — for dropping people, raising land or sending plagues
Forces whole tribes to migrate or hands them food and tools, then lets the consequences run unassisted
Plays back at any speed from half speed to 5000 times, or pauses without losing state
entries.insight: God games usually bury the simulation under quests. The Human Box leaves the agents exposed: reinforcement learning, inherited vocabularies and mutated tribal attitudes are the content, and the 160 tools only change what those agents already react to.

entries.name: Margin
entries.summary: A spacecraft mission design game built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 by an independent team that states plainly it is not a NASA product. You pick an instrument, power, radio, ground stations, orbit and launcher; the game blocks the launch if the numbers do not add up, then flies the mission through the failures you chose.
features: Refuses launch when mass, budget, orbit or structure size do not fit, and warns about power, downlink, memory and pointing margins
Takes orbits, eclipses and ground station passes from NASA GMAT R2025a runs, then simulates the spacecraft in 60-second steps
Lets you decide how many failures may strike, from training runs to none, and shows the ascent in 3D from pad to deployment
Locks hardware, orbit and launcher once you are flying, so redesign happens between missions rather than during one
Ends every run with a report and a design loop: change the spacecraft, launch again
entries.insight: Most space games let you spend an unlimited budget. Margin's teaching value is the constraint it names: it tells you which subsystem fails first, then makes you live with that choice after the fairing separates.

asset.attribution: Margin orbit screenshot from the farfromoffice/margin repository, MIT licensed and unmodified. In-game art also uses NASA public-domain imagery, CC0 Kenney assets and OFL fonts listed in the project credits.
asset.alt: Margin screenshot of a built spacecraft separated and deployed in orbit

entries.name: Frozen-Bubble: SDL3
entries.summary: An independently written rewrite of the 2002 puzzle shooter on SDL3, developed without affiliation to the original project and credited to it in the readme. The aim-and-match loop survives; the multiplayer layer underneath it is rebuilt, with rooms for up to 20 players, bots, tournaments and a public scoreboard.
features: Rewritten in C++ against SDL3, with online rooms for up to 20 players, bots and tournament play
Hosts retune each mode's numbers, and attack bubbles work as on, off or blockable so surplus malus is queued against you
Runs on desktop, Android and Android TV, plus a browser build that plays on phones with no install
Opens a full in-game settings guide from the help button or F1, including how malus targeting changes at six or more live players
Publishes 70 numbered differences from the original, including fixes to the original's own server code
entries.insight: Remakes usually stop at matching the original. This one goes after what the original was weak at — a 20-player room, a maintained scoreboard and a bot model reimplemented against its own board — while publishing the diff from the 2002 game instead of claiming its authorship.

entries.name: Synmergia
entries.summary: A browser-first open-world MMORPG built on Godot 4.7.2 and exported to WebAssembly, on a hand-built 20 km spherical planet with streamed terrain. It is honestly labelled early access: the readme keeps a separate list of what works today and what has not shipped yet, including the player-run market and public launch.
features: Streams a 20 km spherical planet with clipmap terrain, procedural props, player housing and timed world bosses
Offers 18 playable classes across six archetypes and three species, with a skill academy, buffs, arena combat and open-world PvP
Runs guilds with ranks and permissions, parties, raids, friends and ignore lists, chat, territory claims and community governance
Keeps the world alive while you are offline through an authoritative Godot server on a Docker-based shard mesh
Exposes an in-build agent bridge the project uses to test and operate the game world
entries.insight: Browser MMOs normally mean a tile map and a chat window. Synmergia puts a round, streamed planet inside the same tab as a WebAssembly Godot build — and its 'still in progress' list is a more useful guide to an early-access world than most launch trailers.

entries.name: Food Expiration Dates
entries.summary: Keeps a list of what is in your kitchen and shows it in the order it will be thrown away. Adding an item is mostly a barcode scan: the product comes back from the Open Food Facts database, and you only type what the scanner could not find.
features: Sorts food by soonest expiry, with the date you opened a product kept apart from its best-before date
Reads a barcode and fills the item in from the Open Food Facts database
Sends notifications as products approach their dates
Publishes a Google Play build and an IzzyOnDroid F-Droid build with Google services removed
Maintained in 16 languages through a public Weblate project
entries.insight: Fridge inventory apps fail because entering the food costs more effort than the food is worth. Food Expiration Dates removes the typing — a barcode scan and an opening date are enough to get a reminder, which is the only version of this habit that survives a busy week.

entries.name: Aucards

price.label: Completely free, open source and no ads

entries.summary: Turns a phone into a touch board for augmentative and alternative communication: you write a message once, colour its card, then hand the phone over so a single tap opens it fullscreen at speaking size. It is aimed at autistic and ADHD users, people recovering speech, and anyone whose words are hard to get out in the moment.
features: Stores reusable messages as colour-coded cards you can drag into any order or mark as favourites
Opens a tapped card in fullscreen so one message can be shown or read out at distance
Adds optional extra context text underneath the message itself
Edits or deletes a card with a long press, so the board is shaped by its user
Publishes the same package on Google Play and as an F-Droid build
entries.insight: AAC software is usually priced like clinical equipment and locked to one therapy plan. Aucards is a free, offline board anyone can reshape in minutes — which matters most when the person who needs it is the one doing the editing.

entries.name: Eigentone

price.label: Free with no paid tier, ads, account or tracking

entries.summary: A free, open-source equaliser that sits under every app on the phone rather than inside one player, so your headphones and your hearing are corrected once, system wide, without root. Its correction is two-stage: headphone measurements first, then a hearing check that fits the result to you.
features: Applies AutoEq corrections per headphone model, then adds a separate EQ for each ear and a hearing check
Includes reverb, surround and a compressor with nothing held back for a paid tier
Loudness-matches comparisons and bypass, and warns when a setting could clip
Builds its curves on ISO 226:2003 equal-loudness contours, ANSI S3.5 weighting and published Harman listening research
Ships a separate GPL-licensed Windows client alongside the Android app
entries.insight: System-wide EQ on Android is normally a root-only trick or a freemium shell with the useful filters behind a paywall. Eigentone does the unglamorous engineering — per-ear correction and loudness-matched bypass so louder cannot win by accident — and gives all of it away under GPL.

entries.name: TomeVoice
entries.summary: Opens almost any book file you already own and reads it aloud with the voices installed on the phone — EPUB, PDF including scanned pages, DOCX, ODT, MOBI and AZW3, DjVu through its hidden text, and plain text. There is no account, and narration continues with the screen off.
features: Runs Tesseract OCR on scanned PDFs on the device so page images can still be spoken
Reads quoted dialogue in a second voice, with an experimental voice per character
Plays EPUB 3 media overlays when a book already ships its own recorded narration
Highlights the sentence being read and the exact word under the voice
Splits one long TXT web novel into chapters you define, and can swap in a corrected edition of a file
Offers lock-screen playback and roughly 180 optional natural-sounding voices across 42 languages
entries.insight: E-readers treat audiobooks as a separate purchase. TomeVoice treats them as the same file: any EPUB, scanned PDF or page you share from the browser becomes speech on hardware you already own, which is the cheapest route to making a library accessible.

entries.name: Jotsy
entries.summary: A Flutter journal that keeps entries on your device and reads your own history back to you. Each note takes 23 rich-text tools, photos, video, attachments and pauseable recordings, with drafts saved automatically so a half-written page is never lost; backfill, anniversaries and word counts turn the archive into something you can revisit.
features: 23 editor tools including headings, colour, lists and tables, plus multi-image, video, any-type attachments and pauseable audio
Stamps entries with location and weather automatically, with 10 mood emoji and a five-level energy rating
Lists the photos you took on a past date when you backfill that day, so you choose which to insert
Organises notes into journals a single entry can belong to, with tags, search, pinning, archiving and a reversible trash
Adds lunar calendar dates, solar terms, public holidays and repeating anniversaries to month and week views
Exports any card or detail style as a code so layouts can be shared between people
entries.insight: Journal apps optimise the writing moment and forget the reading one. Jotsy builds both halves: capture with weather, mood and location attached, then recovery through lunar-calendar anniversaries, camera-roll backfill and per-entry word counts.

entries.name: Nevumi

price.label: Free, open-source APK, Arch package and AppImage

entries.summary: A Material You music player for Android 12 and Linux, written in Kotlin and Compose, that treats your self-hosted server as the library rather than as a remote folder. Navidrome and Subsonic-compatible servers are browsed, streamed, downloaded, rated and scrobbled through the same API.
features: Streams, downloads, playlists, favourites, ratings and scrobbling over the Subsonic REST API from version 1.13.0
Browses local files by song, album, artist, genre and folder, with artist separators you control
Edits tags and artwork on local files or on Navidrome over SFTP, with MusicBrainz metadata lookups
Adds YouTube Music and SoundCloud on request, contacting YouTube only after you switch it on in Settings
Runs a MilkDrop visualiser built on projectM, with preset packs reproduced from checksum-verified archives
Bundles a tsnet-based Tailscale client so private servers stay private, and ships arm64 and x86_64 APKs from CI
entries.insight: Players that advertise server support usually give you a thin remote view. Nevumi treats the Subsonic API as the library itself — scrobbling, playlist covers written back through Navidrome's native API, SFTP tag editing — which is what makes a self-hosted collection feel local.

asset.attribution: Nevumi home screen from the D3SOX/Nevumi repository packaging, AGPL-3.0 licensed, unmodified. Namida inspired its feature list; no Namida implementation or assets are included.
asset.alt: Nevumi home screen showing library sections on a Material You interface

entries.name: Droynis
entries.summary: An offline security and privacy audit for Android, modelled on Lynis but run on the phone itself: more than 90 read-only checks across device integrity, access control, apps and permissions, network and radios. It holds no INTERNET permission, so nothing it learns can leave the device.
features: Runs 90 plus read-only checks at several privilege levels — base, ADB and Shizuku where you grant them
Scores passed weight against scored weight so a device can be compared over time
Reports a check as unknown when Android will not give up a value, instead of guessing a pass
Mutes checks only the manufacturer can fix and trusts apps that legitimately need wide access
Exports Markdown or JSON reports with personal details hidden by default, and can schedule daily or weekly scans
Checks against a maintained open stalkerware-indicator list without any network access
entries.insight: Phone security tools either demand root or sell you a scan. Droynis borrows Lynis's discipline instead: every check says what it actually read, unknown stays unknown, and the score becomes a diff you can watch between updates — which is what an audit looks like.
